nodes.name: Closing Light
nodes.speaker: Nao
nodes.dialogue: The repair shop looks smaller after midnight, as if the shelves finally exhaled.{pause}One forgotten donation box remains, and the rain has erased our excuse to leave.{pause}The repair lamp quietly warms the counter while rain turns the front glass into silver static.{pause}The shop clock advances with a click much louder than its tiny hands deserve.{pause}A catalog can count objects, but tonight they want it to remember decisions too.

nodes.name: The Heavy Box
nodes.speaker: Miki
nodes.dialogue: Careful with that corner; half these carts survived worse hands than ours.{pause}The other half may be surviving on optimism, old tape, and extremely polite dust.{pause}The repair lamp quietly warms the counter while rain turns the front glass into silver static.{pause}A four-note melody returns, playful enough to keep the late hour from becoming solemn.{pause}Neither of them confuses perfect packaging with proof that a game was loved.

nodes.name: Donation Card
nodes.speaker: Nao
nodes.dialogue: The card says library club, summer years, return what still works.{pause}No donor name appears, only a train time and a blue thumbprint beside it.{pause}The repair lamp quietly warms the counter while rain turns the front glass into silver static.{pause}Miki slides an empty sleeve across the counter like dealing a very careful card.{pause}The box grows lighter while its history grows pleasantly difficult to carry.

nodes.name: First Wake
nodes.speaker: Miki
nodes.dialogue: The first cart clicks, then wakes with a title chime far too cheerful for 12:14.{pause}Its save list holds six names, each followed by the same unfinished summer.{pause}The repair lamp quietly warms the counter while rain turns the front glass into silver static.{pause}Nao writes the time in the margin; midnight deserves accurate witnesses.{pause}Every method reveals something and hides something else; that is why they compare notes.

nodes.name: Six Owners
nodes.speaker: Nao
nodes.dialogue: Yui, Mari, Ken, Toma, Rei, and someone who signed only with a star.{pause}These are not inventory marks; this box belonged to a small rotating club.{pause}The repair lamp quietly warms the counter while rain turns the front glass into silver static.{pause}Plastic cases settle in the box with soft clicks, each one a modest arrival.{pause}They agree that care should leave evidence without sanding away every human trace.

nodes.name: The Old Binder
nodes.speaker: Miki
nodes.dialogue: I found the shop binder from that year, with one page torn cleanly from the rings.{pause}The remaining notes praise a lending box that always returned heavier with stories.{pause}Behind the shop, crowded shelves lean close enough to trade their paper smells.{pause}The test unit glows blue, then dims, as if breathing between borrowed lives.{pause}What began as overtime now feels like being trusted with a very small archive.

nodes.name: Method Matters
nodes.speaker: Nao
nodes.dialogue: If we catalog labels first, we preserve order before tired batteries confuse us.{pause}If we boot or read names first, we may preserve a truer kind of sequence.{pause}Behind the shop, crowded shelves lean close enough to trade their paper smells.{pause}Outside, one bicycle crosses the rain and leaves the whole street quiet again.{pause}The train deadline remains real, but rushing would make the work meaningless.

nodes.name: First Rule
nodes.speaker: Miki
nodes.dialogue: Choose our rule now, while the box is still a mystery and not a project.{pause}The method will decide what we call damage, evidence, and a reason to keep going.{pause}Behind the shop, crowded shelves lean close enough to trade their paper smells.{pause}They pause before the next item, letting the previous story keep its shape.{pause}By morning, the carts need a future, not merely a cleaner description of their past.

nodes.name: Honest Shells
nodes.speaker: Nao
nodes.dialogue: We log sun fade, replacement screws, and tape without grading away their usefulness.{pause}The label order reveals that each owner repaired the cart received from another.{pause}The repair lamp quietly warms the counter while rain turns the front glass into silver static.{pause}The shop clock advances with a click much louder than its tiny hands deserve.{pause}A catalog can count objects, but tonight they want it to remember decisions too.

nodes.name: Blue Parade
nodes.speaker: Miki
nodes.dialogue: We boot every cart, and their title screens form a six-part color sequence.{pause}The sequence spells a locker code through icons no paper catalog would notice.{pause}The repair lamp quietly warms the counter while rain turns the front glass into silver static.{pause}A four-note melody returns, playful enough to keep the late hour from becoming solemn.{pause}Neither of them confuses perfect packaging with proof that a game was loved.

nodes.name: Silver Roll Call
nodes.speaker: Nao
nodes.dialogue: We read every hidden name before cleaning anything that might erase a letter.{pause}The order matches train stops and restores the club route from human evidence.{pause}The repair lamp quietly warms the counter while rain turns the front glass into silver static.{pause}Miki slides an empty sleeve across the counter like dealing a very careful card.{pause}The box grows lighter while its history grows pleasantly difficult to carry.

nodes.name: Silver Yui
nodes.speaker: Miki
nodes.dialogue: A sun-faded puzzle cart says YUI in silver pen under the peeling sticker.{pause}Its save says next summer, which turned out to be a promise the box kept alone.{pause}The repair lamp quietly warms the counter while rain turns the front glass into silver static.{pause}Nao writes the time in the margin; midnight deserves accurate witnesses.{pause}Every method reveals something and hides something else; that is why they compare notes.

nodes.name: Shared Scores
nodes.speaker: Nao
nodes.dialogue: Every title has six scores, never one dominant player and never a blank owner.{pause}They passed each cart around until everyone left a small, imperfect record.{pause}The repair lamp quietly warms the counter while rain turns the front glass into silver static.{pause}Plastic cases settle in the box with soft clicks, each one a modest arrival.{pause}They agree that care should leave evidence without sanding away every human trace.

nodes.name: Bent Manual
nodes.speaker: Miki
nodes.dialogue: A bent manual contains train sketches, snack rankings, and one excellent boss complaint.{pause}The softest part of the collection is also the part no price guide can measure.{pause}Behind the shop, crowded shelves lean close enough to trade their paper smells.{pause}The test unit glows blue, then dims, as if breathing between borrowed lives.{pause}What began as overtime now feels like being trusted with a very small archive.

nodes.name: Repair Note
nodes.speaker: Nao
nodes.dialogue: Mari replaced this battery and wrote, do not erase Toma even if the checksum complains.{pause}The repair was technical, but the reason for it was entirely about friendship.{pause}Behind the shop, crowded shelves lean close enough to trade their paper smells.{pause}Outside, one bicycle crosses the rain and leaves the whole street quiet again.{pause}The train deadline remains real, but rushing would make the work meaningless.

nodes.name: The Club Route
nodes.speaker: Miki
nodes.dialogue: The six names match stops on the late train, one member joining at each station.{pause}By the terminal they had traded every cart and written one line in the binder.{pause}Behind the shop, crowded shelves lean close enough to trade their paper smells.{pause}They pause before the next item, letting the previous story keep its shape.{pause}By morning, the carts need a future, not merely a cleaner description of their past.

nodes.name: Missing Page
nodes.speaker: Nao
nodes.dialogue: The torn page probably listed the final rotation and what became of the club.{pause}Without it, the box is accurate only until the moment accuracy matters most.{pause}Behind the shop, crowded shelves lean close enough to trade their paper smells.{pause}The shop clock advances with a click much louder than its tiny hands deserve.{pause}A catalog can count objects, but tonight they want it to remember decisions too.

nodes.name: Under the Foam
nodes.speaker: Miki
nodes.dialogue: Lift the tray: there is a sealed case beneath it, wrapped in a timetable.{pause}The title is hidden, but six silver initials circle the unopened edge.{pause}Behind the shop, crowded shelves lean close enough to trade their paper smells.{pause}A four-note melody returns, playful enough to keep the late hour from becoming solemn.{pause}Neither of them confuses perfect packaging with proof that a game was loved.

nodes.name: Perfect and Silent
nodes.speaker: Nao
nodes.dialogue: Opening it would end one kind of perfection and begin a much noisier truth.{pause}Leaving it sealed would preserve the club's last agreement without explaining it.{pause}Behind the shop, crowded shelves lean close enough to trade their paper smells.{pause}Miki slides an empty sleeve across the counter like dealing a very careful card.{pause}The box grows lighter while its history grows pleasantly difficult to carry.

nodes.name: Train Time
nodes.speaker: Miki
nodes.dialogue: The donation card's train leaves in twenty minutes, and the sealed case lists that platform.{pause}Either coincidence has excellent typography, or the box expects one final rotation.{pause}The last train hums under them, carrying the catalog toward a pale morning.{pause}Nao writes the time in the margin; midnight deserves accurate witnesses.{pause}Every method reveals something and hides something else; that is why they compare notes.

nodes.name: Platform Locker
nodes.speaker: Nao
nodes.dialogue: At platform four, locker six opens with the club's six initials in order.{pause}Inside waits the missing binder page, dry, flat, and addressed to the next catalogers.{pause}The last train hums under them, carrying the catalog toward a pale morning.{pause}Plastic cases settle in the box with soft clicks, each one a modest arrival.{pause}They agree that care should leave evidence without sanding away every human trace.

nodes.name: Next Catalogers
nodes.speaker: Miki
nodes.dialogue: That is us, apparently; I hoped adulthood would come with less dramatic paperwork.{pause}The page asks us to test the box, keep the names, and choose how it travels.{pause}The last train hums under them, carrying the catalog toward a pale morning.{pause}The test unit glows blue, then dims, as if breathing between borrowed lives.{pause}What began as overtime now feels like being trusted with a very small archive.

nodes.name: Why It Closed
nodes.speaker: Nao
nodes.dialogue: The club ended when their library lost its room, not because the friends fell apart.{pause}They packed one perfect copy as a future starting bell for another shared shelf.{pause}The last train hums under them, carrying the catalog toward a pale morning.{pause}Outside, one bicycle crosses the rain and leaves the whole street quiet again.{pause}The train deadline remains real, but rushing would make the work meaningless.

nodes.name: Nine Minutes
nodes.speaker: Miki
nodes.dialogue: We have nine minutes before our train and enough battery for exactly one decision.{pause}Whatever we do, the box will become a museum, a play log, or a lending route.{pause}The last train hums under them, carrying the catalog toward a pale morning.{pause}They pause before the next item, letting the previous story keep its shape.{pause}By morning, the carts need a future, not merely a cleaner description of their past.

nodes.name: The Sealed Bell
nodes.speaker: Nao
nodes.dialogue: Now the case is not merchandise; it is a bell handed forward by six absent players.{pause}We can keep it sealed, open it, or photograph the promise before choosing both.{pause}The last train hums under them, carrying the catalog toward a pale morning.{pause}The shop clock advances with a click much louder than its tiny hands deserve.{pause}A catalog can count objects, but tonight they want it to remember decisions too.

nodes.name: Six Margins
nodes.speaker: Miki
nodes.dialogue: The missing page leaves six blank margins, one beside every former member's name.{pause}They were not omissions; the club reserved space for strangers who might continue the route.{pause}The last train hums under them, carrying the catalog toward a pale morning.{pause}A four-note melody returns, playful enough to keep the late hour from becoming solemn.{pause}Neither of them confuses perfect packaging with proof that a game was loved.

nodes.name: Nao's First Loan
nodes.speaker: Nao
nodes.dialogue: My first borrowed game came home late because I feared admitting that I had loved it.{pause}A patient librarian renewed it and taught me that care can include an honest delay.{pause}The last train hums under them, carrying the catalog toward a pale morning.{pause}Miki slides an empty sleeve across the counter like dealing a very careful card.{pause}The box grows lighter while its history grows pleasantly difficult to carry.

nodes.name: The Seventh Margin
nodes.speaker: Miki
nodes.dialogue: We write our shop date in the seventh margin before touching the seal or power switch.{pause}Whatever ritual follows, the record will say two tired people accepted responsibility together.{pause}The last train hums under them, carrying the catalog toward a pale morning.{pause}Nao writes the time in the margin; midnight deserves accurate witnesses.{pause}Every method reveals something and hides something else; that is why they compare notes.

nodes.name: A Quiet Bell
nodes.speaker: Nao
nodes.dialogue: I record every edge and leave the seal whole, choosing a traveling museum box.{pause}The club's last game remains silent, but its six names begin speaking elsewhere.{pause}The last train hums under them, carrying the catalog toward a pale morning.{pause}Plastic cases settle in the box with soft clicks, each one a modest arrival.{pause}They agree that care should leave evidence without sanding away every human trace.

nodes.name: The Plastic Sigh
nodes.speaker: Miki
nodes.dialogue: The plastic sighs, the screen crackles, and a bright club anthem fills the train.{pause}We start a shared play log, imperfect now and wonderfully alive again.{pause}The last train hums under them, carrying the catalog toward a pale morning.{pause}The test unit glows blue, then dims, as if breathing between borrowed lives.{pause}What began as overtime now feels like being trusted with a very small archive.

nodes.name: Proof and Play
nodes.speaker: Nao
nodes.dialogue: We photograph the seal, then open carefully and save every ribbon and label.{pause}The box becomes a lending archive with proof of what changed and why.{pause}The last train hums under them, carrying the catalog toward a pale morning.{pause}Outside, one bicycle crosses the rain and leaves the whole street quiet again.{pause}The train deadline remains real, but rushing would make the work meaningless.

nodes.name: Good End: Traveling Museum
nodes.speaker: Nao
nodes.dialogue: The last train hums under them, carrying the catalog toward a pale morning.{pause}They pause before the next item, letting the previous story keep its shape.{pause}By morning, the carts need a future, not merely a cleaner description of their past.{pause}Our condition cards make the unopened box useful without pretending silence is play.{pause}Each host library adds a date, and the six-owner sequence remains intact.

nodes.name: Good End: Blue Sequence
nodes.speaker: Miki
nodes.dialogue: The last train hums under them, carrying the catalog toward a pale morning.{pause}The shop clock advances with a click much louder than its tiny hands deserve.{pause}A catalog can count objects, but tonight they want it to remember decisions too.{pause}We preserve the sealed bell but tour the six playable carts in their recovered order.{pause}Every title chime leads toward the quiet seventh case like a respectful countdown.

nodes.name: Good End: Silver Roll Call
nodes.speaker: Nao
nodes.dialogue: The last train hums under them, carrying the catalog toward a pale morning.{pause}A four-note melody returns, playful enough to keep the late hour from becoming solemn.{pause}Neither of them confuses perfect packaging with proof that a game was loved.{pause}The sealed case rests beside six enlarged name cards, never reduced to market value.{pause}At every stop, a new club reads the old roll before adding its own.

nodes.name: Good End: Living Catalog
nodes.speaker: Miki
nodes.dialogue: The last train hums under them, carrying the catalog toward a pale morning.{pause}Miki slides an empty sleeve across the counter like dealing a very careful card.{pause}The box grows lighter while its history grows pleasantly difficult to carry.{pause}The opened anthem joins a catalog that records every repaired edge and honest scar.{pause}Nothing is mint, everything works, and the midnight box finally exhales.

nodes.name: Good End: Play Log Dawn
nodes.speaker: Miki
nodes.dialogue: The last train hums under them, carrying the catalog toward a pale morning.{pause}Nao writes the time in the margin; midnight deserves accurate witnesses.{pause}Every method reveals something and hides something else; that is why they compare notes.{pause}We play all seven in sequence and write one unruly line after every title screen.{pause}The first says tested at 4:12; the second says laughed before the train moved.

nodes.name: Good End: Seventh Name
nodes.speaker: Nao
nodes.dialogue: The last train hums under them, carrying the catalog toward a pale morning.{pause}Plastic cases settle in the box with soft clicks, each one a modest arrival.{pause}They agree that care should leave evidence without sanding away every human trace.{pause}After opening, we keep the six saves and add the shop as a seventh careful owner.{pause}The box returns to lending with its human order protected inside every case.

nodes.name: Good End: Proof Box
nodes.speaker: Nao
nodes.dialogue: The last train hums under them, carrying the catalog toward a pale morning.{pause}The test unit glows blue, then dims, as if breathing between borrowed lives.{pause}What began as overtime now feels like being trusted with a very small archive.{pause}Before each loan, the archive shows exactly what was sealed, opened, and repaired.{pause}Care becomes visible labor instead of a claim printed on a grading label.

nodes.name: Good End: Borrowed Anthem
nodes.speaker: Miki
nodes.dialogue: The last train hums under them, carrying the catalog toward a pale morning.{pause}Outside, one bicycle crosses the rain and leaves the whole street quiet again.{pause}The train deadline remains real, but rushing would make the work meaningless.{pause}The photographed seal travels with a test log and the newly audible club anthem.{pause}Borrowers return the box with scores, jokes, and batteries that are never quite full.

nodes.name: Good End: Next Summer
nodes.speaker: Nao
nodes.dialogue: The last train hums under them, carrying the catalog toward a pale morning.{pause}They pause before the next item, letting the previous story keep its shape.{pause}By morning, the carts need a future, not merely a cleaner description of their past.{pause}We place Yui's silver promise first and invite six new names onto a removable card.{pause}The old writing stays untouched while next summer finally receives an answer.
